**TL;DR**

- **The AI-capex trade broke, and the market drew the line there.** The S&P 500 closed **7,580.07 −1.82%** and the Nasdaq Composite **25,437.00 −2.86%** —
- the Composite's worst day since 5 June — while the Dow fell only **1.09% to 51,770.31** and the equal-weight S&P fell just **0.79%**.
- **RSP −0.79% against SPY −1.77% is a 99bp cap-weight penalty** (yesterday it was a 158bp *bonus* to the equal weight). The damage was concentrated: **Intel −28.58% to $65.76** —
- its steepest one-day drop on record — and the **PHLX Semiconductor Index −7.20% to 10,688.80**, its worst day since 5 June, with 29 of 30 constituents lower.
- **Breadth was genuinely bad, not a one-stock scare.** In the liquid universe (cap > $200M, vol > 100k) only **939 names advanced against 2,262 decliners — 0.42:1** —
- and **563 names fell more than 5%**. The **11 sector ETFs split 5 up / 5 down**, but the split was not gentle:
- **XLK −4.89%** and **SMH −6.98%** versus **XLE +1.91%**, **XLP +1.41%**, **XLU +0.67%**, **XLV +0.45%**, **XLRE +0.26%**.
- Money left the AI complex and did not fully rotate in — it went to energy, staples and cash.
- **Three separate shocks landed in 24 hours, and the fourth came on Friday afternoon.** Amazon's **−$42.4B trailing FCF**, Intel's guidance and Alphabet's **−$9.07B FCF** form one story —
- the market is repricing what AI capex returns.
- On Friday it added **Blackstone's warning that Anthropic will likely get a junk credit rating** post-IPO, **a $6.3B Binance hack** that took bitcoin to a six-week low, and **gold to a one-year low** with GLD **−3.47%**.
- The 2-year **fell 5bp to 4.56%** and the 10-year **4bp to 4.94%** — a genuine flight to quality inside a selloff.
- **The volatility market is the real warning, not the equity tape.** **VIX 19.42 +12.91%** (prior 17.20) after touching **23.93 intraday** —
- a **29.8% spike off the open** that then faded 18.8% into the close. **VXN 28.50 +13.19%**, so the Nasdaq vol premium over VIX widened from **7.98 to 9.08 points**.
- The VIX/VIX3M ratio was **0.9346** versus 0.8880 — still contango, but the cushion is nearly gone.
- Total put/call **0.90** with equity put/call **0.66** shows no broad hedging rush; this was a concentrated repricing of the AI complex.
- **Next week is the hard part.** **Apple reports after Monday's close** , the **US midterms are Tuesday 3 November** ,
- ISM manufacturing lands Monday 10:00 ET, and the October jobs report is Friday 6 November.
- The weekend has no cash session and the Globex futures market is closed until Sunday 18:00 ET —
- so the first read on whether Monday gaps down will come from the crypto and Asia sessions, not from futures.

*Reference: SMH 522.49, −6.98%. SOXX 471.51, −8.24%. PHLX Semiconductor Index 10,688.80, −7.20%.*

- **Read:** this was **a de-rating of the AI complex, not a general risk-off session**, and the two are distinguished by three facts.
- First, the Dow fell a third as much as the Nasdaq and the Russell 2000 *rose* on the week.
- Second, **every sector that fell did so for a specific reason** —
- Technology because of the chip complex, Industrials because of the capex read-through, Communication Services because Alphabet is 22% of it.
- Third, and most telling, **Financials fell 0.76% with 810 decliners against 351 advancers** — the broadest sector in the index was sold too.
- When defensives, energy and financials all go down together with tech, that is a liquidity event, not a rotation.
- The breadth column is the tell: **11 of 12 GICS sectors had more decliners than advancers**, including all five of the day's winners.

**Confirmed catalysts for the top of the move list:**

- **CDNA +22.22%** — Q3 revenue **$139.36M vs $121.96M est (+39% y/y)**, adjusted EPS **$0.70 vs $0.26**; GAAP net income $19M vs $2M;
- adjusted EBITDA **doubled to $30M**, nearly matching all of 2025. **FY26 revenue guidance raised to $520–530M from $490–500M** and adjusted EBITDA to **$90–100M from $66–78M**.
- Testing Services revenue $119M (+65%); testing volume 75,900 (+51%).
- **But $15M of the quarter was catch-up from tests run in earlier periods** (vs $6M a year ago) — ex-catch-up, Testing Services grew ~58%.
- Cash from operations fell to $13M from $37M. Canaccord raised its target to $80 from $65; BTIG to $81 from $74, then to $92.
- **Natera reports next week** — its Prospera test competes directly with AlloSure.
- **CPRI +16.31%** — Capri Holdings Q2 FY27: **revenue, operating income and EPS all exceeded expectations**, full-year outlook raised.
- Total revenue $809M, **−5.5% reported / −4.9% constant currency**, but **~$20M was an earlier-than-anticipated wholesale shipment timing**, which is what management called out.
- Adjusted EPS $0.42; operating margin 1.2%, adjusted 3.8%. **Jimmy Choo revenue $325M, +10.9%**. $150M of buybacks at an average $14.56.
- **FDXF +14.91%** — FedEx Freight transition-period results, October 29: **raised its adjusted operating income forecast** while reporting lower operating income and diluted EPS. A $16.4B market value on 149.5M shares.
- **REGN +13.33%** — the full beat, detailed in the leaders table above. New 52-week high; guidance raised for R&D to $6.60–6.74B and capex to $1.05–1.10B.
- EYLEA (2mg) US sales fell 41% y/y to $400M with a low-to-mid-teens sequential decline expected in Q4.
- **GPN +12.97%** — **not earnings.** The stock jumped on a report that **CD&R is pursuing a takeover** (TipRanks, 13:28 ET), and the analyst wave followed:
- **Oppenheimer to Outperform/$115, BofA to Buy/$114 (reinstated), KeyBanc to Overweight/$105**, Goldman $98. GPN reports Q3 on 5 November.
- **BTSG +11.08%** — Q3 revenue **$4.213B, +26.4%** (vs $3.334B), adjusted EPS **$0.54 vs $0.47**, adjusted EBITDA **$228M, +42%**, net income from continuing operations $101M vs $38M.
- **Full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance raised** to $15.9–16.125B and $850–860M. Specialty and infusion revenue +34%; home-health census +58%. Offset: a **~$50M quarterly IRA impact** on home and community pharmacy.
- **MEOH +14.04%**, **GDDY +10.72%**, **OLN +9.66%**, **INTA +7.95%**, **HGV +7.64%**, **RKT +7.38%**, **MHK +7.25%**, **CSGP +7.21%**, **MIAX +6.97%** — no catalyst confirmed in this run. Treated as unconfirmed.

- **BFAM −17.92%**, **TFII −17.08%**, **BLSH −16.05%**, **AUGO −15.43%**, **TXG −14.03%**, **AAOI −12.80%**, **TWST −11.92%**, **GLXY −11.75%**, **PENG −11.67%** — no catalyst confirmed in this run.
- **XOM +2.16% and CVX +1.75%** — energy earnings beats on strong margins (the oil read matters as much for the inflation path as for the stocks).
- **ABOS −90.83% to $0.21** — the day's most severe clinical repricing.
- The 542-participant Phase 2 **ALTITUDE-AD trial of sabirnetug (ACU193) failed its primary endpoint** (iADRS at 18 months, both doses) and key secondaries including CDR-SB.
- Amyloid plaques fell significantly but that did not translate into clinical benefit. **Acumen is ceasing development** and moving to cash conservation and strategic alternatives. ARIA-E in ~10% of treated patients.
- Cantor Fitzgerald downgraded to Underweight.
- **PGEN −23.63% after hours** —
- Precigen closed the regular session **up 4.52% to $6.94**, then fell to **$5.30** in extended trading on **no company news** (its Q3 is not due until 4 November).
- Public discussion points to the **Inovio FDA approval as a competitive read-through** —
- INO-3107/Voceryq is approved for the same recurrent respiratory papillomatosis indication Precigen's PAPZIMEOS targets, and a Yahoo comment thread explicitly links the two.
- The after-hours print is unstable across venues ($5.15 at 03:14 per Investing.com, $4.82 at 17:22 per Yahoo, $5.30 at 20:00 per MarketChameleon), so treat the exact level as provisional.
- **Do not treat this as a confirmed catalyst.**

**5. After-hours earnings reactions**

**Intel (INTC) — **−28.58% to $65.76** — a good quarter and a catastrophic guide**

- Q3 adjusted EPS **$0.52 vs $0.40–0.41 expected** (FactSet $0.41; Earnings Whisper $0.47); revenue **$16.51B vs $16.50B expected, +21% y/y**.
- **Data center and AI revenue $7.3B, +78%** — the strongest data-center growth in 15 years, above the $6.6B projected.
- **Q4 guide $15.0–16.0B vs a ~$17.1B consensus**; adj. EPS guide **$0.25 vs $0.42–0.45**; GAAP gross margin guided to **37.1% from 43%**.
- CFO David Zinsner: "**We see the PC slowdown continuing at least the first half of next year.**" PC chip sales **$8.1B vs an $8.8B target**. Investrade:
- Q3 PC revenue missed by $800M and was guided down more than 20% q/q in Q4, over $2B below consensus, on an accelerating PC inventory correction (CCPG down >20% q/q).
- An **explosion at an Israeli fab** accounts for roughly **$300M** of the Q4 miss.
- The stock had been up ~150% YTD before the print.
- **CNBC/TipRanks: "steepest one-day drop on record."** The after-hours print was **$64.89, −1.32%** on 41.1M shares — the selling continued into the extended session rather than reversing.

**The AI-financing story widened on Friday afternoon — the intraday trigger**

- **Blackstone now expects Anthropic to receive a junk (BB-range) credit rating after its IPO**, reversing its earlier guidance that Anthropic could reach investment grade by year-end (FT report, 30 October).
- Blackstone's funds hold **$9B of the $18B junior tranche of the $63B "Project North Star" financing**, bought at yields above 10%; $42B of senior debt is guaranteed by Broadcom.
- **KBRA assigned Anthropic BB+ in June — a rating that stayed unreported until Friday** and was disclosed via an 8-K-adjacent review by the FT.
- **Microsoft priced a $25B bond sale** — its first major US bond deal since 2017 — to fund AI expansion, at roughly 64bp over Treasuries.
- Anthropic's S-1 discloses **US$321B of leases not yet commenced** as of 30 June, up from ~$50B at 31 December, **$6.2B of current debt** (Amazon convertible notes) and the option to issue up to **$42B** more to Broadcom.
- **Investrade attributes the midafternoon leg lower in semis specifically to the Anthropic junk-rating report.** That timing matches the tape:
- the SOX was down 6.30% at 10:58 ET and closed down 7.20%.

- **What the breadth actually says.** This was **the broadest, most violent single-session deterioration of the year**, and the equal-weight cushion was the only thing keeping it from worse.
- **563 names fell more than 5%** and **1,242 fell more than 2%** —
- in a universe of 3,245 liquid names, that is roughly one in three names down double digits on the day.
- Even the megacaps were net negative (176 advancers against 247 decliners among names over $40B). And the sector breadth is the part that argues against calling this a rotation:
- **all five of the day's winning sectors had more decliners than advancers inside them.** Energy's XLE was +1.91% on 93 advancers against 90 decliners;
- Consumer Staples' XLP was +1.41% on 92 against 61. A sector ETF up on a coin-flip breadth is a handful of large caps carrying an index, not a bid.
- What the tape actually shows is **liquidity leaving the AI complex and not fully arriving anywhere**.

- **What the vol market says.** The volatility surface is the sharper warning. **VIX 9-day at 19.25 rose 21.30% while VIX rose 12.91% and VIX3M rose only 7.28%** —
- the front of the curve repriced hardest, which is what an event-risk session looks like. **VIX/VIX3M at 0.9346** is still contango, but the cushion has fallen from 12.6% to 7.0%:
- the market is paying up for near-term risk and is no longer being paid to wait. The **intraday path matters more than the close**:
- VIX ran from an 18.43 open to a 23.93 high — a 29.8% spike — and then gave back 18.8% into the close at 19.42.
- That fade says the market stabilised, and the after-hours tape agrees (SPY +0.19%, QQQ +0.33%, SMH +0.81%, and no mega-cap after-hours gap in either direction).
- Total put/call of 0.90 and equity put/call of 0.66 show **no broad hedging rush** — this was concentrated repricing of a complex, not a de-risking of the market.

- The credit channel is now a live transmission mechanism for AI risk and it has not been priced.
